sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第164卷卷第一百六十四

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 164, Roll 164
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 164

sentences.zh: 【梁紀二十】　起重光協洽，盡玄黓涒灘，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 20] From Chongguang Xieqia through Xuanyi Youtan; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 20] From Chongguang Xieqia through Xuanyi Youtan—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝下大寶二年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Jianwen, lower scroll, second year of Dabao (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen of Liang, second year of Dabao (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元五五一年）

translations.literal: xinwei, 551 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei, AD 551)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，新吳余孝頃舉兵拒侯景，景遣于慶攻之，不克。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yu Xiaoqing of Xinwu raised troops to resist Hou Jing; Jing sent Yu Qing to attack him and could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yu Xiaoqing of Xinwu raised troops against Hou Jing. Jing sent Yu Qing to attack him but failed to break him.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，湘東王繹遣護軍將軍尹悅、安東將軍杜幼安、巴州刺史王珣將兵二萬自江夏趣武昌，受徐文盛節度。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Guard-General Yin Yue, Pacification-East General Du You'an, and Bazhou Inspector Wang Xun with twenty thousand men from Jiangxia toward Wuchang, under Xu Wensheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent guard-general Yin Yue, pacification-east general Du You'an, and Bazhou inspector Wang Xun with twenty thousand men from Jiangxia toward Wuchang, under Xu Wensheng's command.

sentences.zh: 楊乾運攻拔劍閣，楊法琛退保石門，乾運據南陰平。

translations.literal: Yang Qianyun stormed and took Jiange; Yang Fachen withdrew to hold Shimen; Qianyun seized Southern Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qianyun stormed and took Jiange. Yang Fachen withdrew to Shimen while Qianyun seized Southern Yinping.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，齊主祀圜丘。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Qi ruler sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Qi emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 張彪遣其將趙稜圍錢塘，孫鳳圍富春，侯景遣儀同三司田遷、趙伯超救之，稜、鳳敗走。

translations.literal: Zhang Biao sent his generals Zhao Ling to besiege Qiantang and Sun Feng to besiege Fuchun; Hou Jing sent Masters of Protocol Tian Qian and Zhao Bochao to rescue them; Ling and Feng were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao sent Zhao Ling to besiege Qiantang and Sun Feng to besiege Fuchun. Hou Jing sent masters of protocol Tian Qian and Zhao Bochao to relieve them. Ling and Feng were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 稜，伯超之兄子也。

translations.literal: Ling was Bochao's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was the son of Bochao's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，齊主耕籍田。

translations.literal: On guihai, the Qi ruler plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Qi emperor plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，享太廟。

translations.literal: On yichou, he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 魏楊忠圍汝南，李素戰死。

translations.literal: Wei Yang Zhong besieged Runan; Li Su died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong of Wei besieged Runan; Li Su fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，城陷，執邵陵攜王綸，殺之，投屍江岸；

translations.literal: In the second month, on yihai, the city fell; they seized Prince of Shaoling Lun, the hostage prince, killed him, and cast his corpse on the riverbank;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai, the city fell. They seized Prince Lun of Shaoling, the hostage prince, killed him, and cast his body on the riverbank;

sentences.zh: 岳陽王察取而葬之。

translations.literal: Prince of Yueyang Cha took it and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cha of Yueyang recovered the body and buried him.

sentences.zh: 或告齊太尉彭樂謀反；

translations.literal: Someone reported that Qi Grand Commandant Peng Yue plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Qi grand commandant Peng Yue was plotting rebellion;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，樂坐誅。

translations.literal: on renchen, Yue was executed for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: on renchen, Yue was executed.

sentences.zh: 齊遣散騎常侍曹文皎使於江陵，湘東王繹使兼散騎常侍王子敏報之。

translations.literal: Qi sent Palace Attendant Cao Wenjiao as envoy to Jiangling; Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Concurrent Palace Attendant Wang Zimin in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent palace attendant Cao Wenjiao to Jiangling; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent concurrent palace attendant Wang Zimin in reply.

sentences.zh: 侯景以王克為太師，宋子仙為太保，元羅為太傅，郭元建為太尉，支化仁為司徒，任約為司空，王偉為尚書左僕射，索超世為右僕射。

translations.literal: Hou Jing made Wang Ke Grand Preceptor, Song Zixian Grand Guardian, Yuan Luo Grand Tutor, Guo Yuanjian Grand Commandant, Zhi Huaren Minister of Education, Ren Yue Minister of Works, Wang Wei Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Suo Chaoshi Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing made Wang Ke grand preceptor, Song Zixian grand guardian, Yuan Luo grand tutor, Guo Yuanjian grand commandant, Zhi Huaren minister of education, Ren Yue minister of works, Wang Wei left vice director of the masters of writing, and Suo Chaoshi right vice director.

sentences.zh: 景置三公官，動以十數，儀同尤多。

translations.literal: Jing established the Three Dukes' offices by the tens, and Masters of Protocol were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Jing created Three Dukes' posts by the dozen, and masters of protocol were especially thick on the ground.

sentences.zh: 以子仙、元建、化仁為佐命元功，偉、超世為謀主，於子悅、彭雋主擊斷，陳慶、呂季略、盧暉略、丁和等為爪牙。

translations.literal: He took Zixian, Yuanjian, and Huaren as founding merit of co-rule, Wei and Chaoshi as chief strategists, Yu Ziyue and Peng Juan as masters of judgment, and Chen Qing, Lü Jilüe, Lu Huilüe, Ding He, and others as claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian, Yuanjian, and Huaren were his founding merit; Wei and Chaoshi were chief strategists; Yu Ziyue and Peng Juan held judgment; Chen Qing, Lü Jilüe, Lu Huilüe, Ding He, and others were his claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 梁人為景用者，則故將軍趙伯超，前制局監周石珍，內監嚴但，邵陵王記室伏知命。

translations.literal: Liang men Jing employed were former general Zhao Bochao, former Bureau of Manufactures supervisor Zhou Shizhen, inner attendant Yan Dan, and Prince of Shaoling's recorder Fu Zhiming.
translations.idiomatic: Among Liang men in Jing's service were former general Zhao Bochao, former bureau of manufactures supervisor Zhou Shizhen, inner attendant Yan Dan, and Prince Lun of Shaoling's recorder Fu Zhiming.

sentences.zh: 自餘王克、元羅及侍中殷不害、太常周弘正等，景從人望，加以尊位，非腹心之任也。

translations.literal: As for the rest—Wang Ke, Yuan Luo, Palace Attendant Yin Buhai, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Zhou Hongzheng, and the like—Jing followed men's repute and gave them honored posts, but they were not trusted inner duties.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest—Wang Ke, Yuan Luo, palace attendant Yin Buhai, chamberlain for ceremonials Zhou Hongzheng, and the like—Jing followed public esteem and gave them honored posts, but they were not trusted inner duties.

sentences.zh: 北兗州刺史蕭邕謀降魏，侯景殺之。

translations.literal: Northern Yanzhou Inspector Xiao Yong plotted to surrender to Wei; Hou Jing killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Yanzhou inspector Xiao Yong plotted to surrender to Wei; Hou Jing killed him.

sentences.zh: 楊乾運進據平興，平興者，楊法琛所治也。

translations.literal: Yang Qianyun advanced and seized Pingxing; Pingxing was what Yang Fachen governed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qianyun advanced and seized Pingxing, which Yang Fachen had governed.

sentences.zh: 法琛退保魚石洞，乾運焚平興而歸。

translations.literal: Fachen withdrew to hold Yushi Cave; Qianyun burned Pingxing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fachen withdrew to Yushi Cave; Qianyun burned Pingxing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李遷仕收眾還擊南康，陳霸先遣其將杜僧明等拒之，生擒遷仕，斬之。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi gathered his followers and returned to strike Nankang; Chen Baxian sent his generals Du Sengming and others to resist, captured Qianshi alive, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi gathered his men and struck at Nankang. Chen Baxian sent Du Sengming and others against him, took Qianshi alive, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹使霸先進兵取江州，以為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi had Baxian advance to take Jiang province and made him Jiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong had Baxian advance to take Jiang province and made him Jiangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙午，齊襄城王淯卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingwu, Prince of Xiangcheng You died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingwu, Prince You of Xiangcheng died.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏文帝殂，太子欽立。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wei Emperor Wen died; the crown prince Qin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Emperor Wen of Wei died; crown prince Qin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，徐文盛等克武昌，進軍蘆洲。

translations.literal: On yimao, Xu Wensheng and others took Wuchang and advanced to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Xu Wensheng and others took Wuchang and advanced to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 己未，齊以湘東王繹為梁相國，建梁台，總百揆，承製。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Qi made Prince of Xiangdong Yi Liang's Chancellor of State, raised the Liang headquarters, oversaw the hundred duties, and acted by regent's order.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Qi made Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong chancellor of state for Liang, raised the Liang headquarters, oversaw the hundred duties, and acted by regent's order.

sentences.zh: 齊司空司馬子如自求封王，齊主怒，庚申，免子如官。

translations.literal: Qi Minister of Works Sima Ziru asked to be enfeoffed as prince; the Qi ruler was angry; on gengshen he removed Ziru from office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi minister of works Sima Ziru asked to be enfeoffed as prince. The Qi emperor was furious; on gengshen he stripped Ziru of office.

sentences.zh: 任約告急，侯景自帥眾西上，攜太子大器從軍以為質，留王偉居守。

translations.literal: Ren Yue reported in emergency; Hou Jing himself led troops west, taking crown prince Daqi with the army as hostage, and left Wang Wei to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue called for help. Hou Jing himself led troops west, taking crown prince Daqi with the army as hostage, and left Wang Wei to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 閏月，景發建康，自石頭至新林，舳艫相接。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Jing set out from Jiankang; from Shitou to Xinlin, ships and boats linked stem to stern.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Jing marched from Jiankang. From Shitou to Xinlin, ships lay stem to stern.

sentences.zh: 約分兵襲破定州刺史田龍祖於齊安。

translations.literal: Yue detached troops and in a raid broke Dingzhou Inspector Tian Longzu at Qi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yue detached troops and routed Dingzhou inspector Tian Longzu at Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，景軍至西陽，與徐文盛夾江築壘。

translations.literal: On renyin, Jing's army reached Xiyang and built ramparts on both banks of the river facing Xu Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Jing's army reached Xiyang and built ramparts on both banks facing Xu Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，文盛擊破之，射其右丞庫狄式和墜水死，景遁走還營。

translations.literal: On guimao, Wensheng struck and broke them, shot his right aide Kudi Shihe so that he fell into the water and died; Jing fled back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Wensheng routed them, shot his right aide Kudi Shihe into the river to his death; Jing fled back to camp.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，魏葬文帝於永陵。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, Wei buried Emperor Wen at Yongling.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, Wei buried Emperor Wen at Yongling.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史蕭方諸，年十五，以行事鮑泉和弱，常侮易之，或使伏床，騎背為馬；

translations.literal: Yingzhou Inspector Xiao Fangzhu, fifteen years old, because acting administrator Bao Quan was mild and weak, often insulted and belittled him, sometimes made him lie face down on a bed and rode his back as a horse;
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou inspector Xiao Fangzhu was fifteen. Because acting administrator Bao Quan was mild and weak, he often bullied him, sometimes made him lie on a bed, and rode his back as a horse;

sentences.zh: 恃徐文盛軍在近，不復設備，日以蒲酒為樂。

translations.literal: relying on Xu Wensheng's army being near, he no longer made preparations and passed his days in reed-wine pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: trusting that Xu Wensheng's army was near, he stopped preparing defenses and spent his days in reed-wine pleasure.

sentences.zh: 侯景聞江夏空虛，乙巳，使宋子仙、任約帥精騎四百，由淮內襲郢州。

translations.literal: Hou Jing heard Jiangxia was empty; on yisi he sent Song Zixian and Ren Yue leading four hundred picked horsemen through the Huai interior to strike Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing heard Jiangxia was undefended. On yisi he sent Song Zixian and Ren Yue with four hundred picked horsemen through the Huai interior to strike Ying province.

sentences.zh: 丙午，大風疾雨，天色晦冥，有登陴望見賊者，告泉曰：「虜騎至矣！

translations.literal: On bingwu, great wind and driving rain; the sky was dark; someone who climbed the wall and saw the enemy reported to Quan: "The barbarian horsemen have come!
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu came great wind and driving rain; the sky went black. Someone who climbed the wall and saw the enemy told Quan: "The enemy horsemen are here!

sentences.zh: 」泉曰：「徐文盛大軍在下，賊何因得至！

translations.literal: " Quan said: "Xu Wensheng's great army is downstream—how could the enemy get here!
translations.idiomatic: " Quan said: "Xu Wensheng's main force is downstream—how could the enemy get here!

sentences.zh: 當是王珣軍人還耳。

translations.literal: It must be Wang Xun's troops returning.
translations.idiomatic: It must be Wang Xun's men returning.

sentences.zh: 」既而走告者稍眾，始命閉門，子仙等已入城。

translations.literal: " Before long those who came running to report grew numerous; only then did he order the gates closed—but Zixian and the others were already inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long more runners came; only then did he order the gates shut—but Zixian and the others were already inside.

sentences.zh: 方諸方踞泉腹，以五色彩辮其髯；

translations.literal: Fangzhu was just sitting astride Quan's belly, braiding his beard with five-colored threads;
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhu was sitting astride Quan's belly, braiding his beard with five-colored thread;

sentences.zh: 見子仙至，方諸迎拜，泉匿於床下；

translations.literal: when he saw Zixian arrive, Fangzhu rose to bow in welcome; Quan hid under the bed;
translations.idiomatic: when Zixian arrived, Fangzhu rose to bow; Quan hid under the bed;

sentences.zh: 子仙俯窺見泉素髯間彩，驚愕，遂擒之，及司馬虞豫，送於景所。

translations.literal: Zixian bent down, peered in, saw Quan's plain beard threaded with color, was startled, seized him, and also Chief Clerk Yu Yu, and sent them to Jing's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian bent down, saw Quan's plain beard threaded with color, seized him in shock, and also chief clerk Yu Yu, and sent both to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景因便風，中江舉帆，遂越文盛等軍。

translations.literal: Jing caught a favorable wind, raised sail mid-river, and thus passed ahead of Wensheng's army and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Jing caught a fair wind, raised sail mid-river, and swept past Wensheng's army.

sentences.zh: 丁未，入江夏。

translations.literal: On dingwei, he entered Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, he entered Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 文盛眾懼而潰，與長沙王韶等逃歸江陵。

translations.literal: Wensheng's troops feared and broke; with Prince of Changsha Shao and others he fled back to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng's men panicked and broke. With Prince Shao of Changsha and others he fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 珣、杜幼安以家在江夏，遂降於景。

translations.literal: Xun and Du You'an, because their families were in Jiangxia, then surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Du You'an, whose families were in Jiangxia, surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹以王僧辯為大都督，帥巴州刺史丹楊淳於量、定州刺史杜龕、宜州刺史王琳、郴州刺史裴之橫東擊景，徐文盛以下並受節度。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi made Wang Senbian Grand Commander, leading Bazhou Inspector Chunyu Liang of Danyang, Dingzhou Inspector Du Kan, Yizhou Inspector Wang Lin, and Chenzhou Inspector Pei Zhiheng east to strike Jing; Xu Wensheng and those below all accepted his command.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made Wang Senbian grand commander, leading Bazhou inspector Chunyu Liang of Danyang, Dingzhou inspector Du Kan, Yizhou inspector Wang Lin, and Chenzhou inspector Pei Zhiheng east against Jing; Xu Wensheng and all below accepted his command.

sentences.zh: 戊申，僧辯等軍至巴陵，聞郢州已陷，因留戍之。

translations.literal: On wushen, Senbian's army and the rest reached Baling; hearing Ying province had fallen, they therefore remained to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Senbian reached Baling. Hearing Ying province had fallen, he halted to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 繹遺僧辯書曰：「賊既乘勝，必將西下，不勞遠擊；

translations.literal: Yi sent Senbian a letter saying: "The rebels, having ridden victory, are sure to come west downstream—no need for a distant strike;
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote Senbian: "The rebels, riding victory, are sure to come west—no need to chase them far;

sentences.zh: 但守巴丘，以逸待勞，無慮不克。

translations.literal: only hold Baling, meet weariness with rest, and there is no worry of failure.
translations.idiomatic: only hold Baling, meet their weariness with your rest, and you cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」又謂僚佐曰：「景若水步兩道，直指江陵，此上策也；

translations.literal: " He also told his staff: "If Jing takes both water and land routes straight at Jiangling, that is the upper plan;
translations.idiomatic: " He also told his staff: "If Jing takes both river and land straight at Jiangling, that is the best plan;

sentences.zh: 據夏首，積兵糧，中策也；

translations.literal: to hold Xiakou and stock troops and grain is the middle plan;
translations.idiomatic: to hold Xiakou and stock troops and grain is the middle plan;

sentences.zh: 悉力攻巴陵，下策也。

translations.literal: to throw all strength at Baling is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: to throw everything at Baling is the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 巴陵城小而固，僧辯足可委任。

translations.literal: Baling's walls are small but firm; Senbian is fully fit to be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Baling is small but strong; Senbian is fully fit to hold it.

sentences.zh: 景攻城不拔，野無所掠，暑疫時起，食盡兵疲，破之必矣。

translations.literal: If Jing besieges and cannot take it, the countryside offers nothing to plunder, summer pestilence rises in season, food runs out and troops weary—breaking him is certain.
translations.idiomatic: If Jing cannot take it, the countryside offers nothing to plunder, summer pestilence will rise, food will run out and his men will weary—then he is finished.

sentences.zh: 」乃命羅州刺史徐嗣徽自岳陽、武州刺史杜崱自武陵引兵會僧辯。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Luozhou Inspector Xu Sihui from Yueyang and Wuzhou Inspector Du Xi from Wuling to lead troops and join Senbian.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Luozhou inspector Xu Sihui from Yueyang and Wuzhou inspector Du Xi from Wuling to bring troops and join Senbian.

sentences.zh: 景使丁和將兵五千守夏首，宋子仙將兵一萬為前驅，趣巴陵，分遣任約直指江陵，景帥大兵水步繼進。

translations.literal: Jing sent Ding He with five thousand men to hold Xiakou, Song Zixian with ten thousand as vanguard hurrying to Baling, detached Ren Yue straight at Jiangling, and Jing himself led the main force by water and land in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Ding He with five thousand to hold Xiakou and Song Zixian with ten thousand as vanguard for Baling, detached Ren Yue straight at Jiangling, and followed with the main force by river and road.

sentences.zh: 於是緣江戍邏，望風請服，景拓邏至於隱磯。

translations.literal: Thus along the river the garrison posts, seeing the wind, asked to submit; Jing extended his patrols to Yinjii.
translations.idiomatic: Along the river the garrisons submitted at the first rumor; Jing extended his patrols to Yinjii.

sentences.zh: 僧辯乘城固守，偃旗臥鼓，安若無人。

translations.literal: Senbian manned the walls and held firm, lowered banners and stilled drums, calm as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian held the walls, lowered banners and stilled drums, calm as if the city were empty.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，景眾濟江，遣輕騎至城下，問：「城內為誰？

translations.literal: On renxu, Jing's host crossed the river and sent light horse to the wall, asking: "Who is inside the city?
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Jing's host crossed the river and sent light horse to the wall: "Who holds this city?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「王領軍。

translations.literal: " The answer came: "Commander Wang.
translations.idiomatic: " Came the answer: "Commander Wang.

sentences.zh: 」騎曰：「何不早降？

translations.literal: " The horseman said: "Why not surrender early?
translations.idiomatic: " The horseman said: "Why not surrender now?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯曰：「大軍但向荊州，此城自當非礙。

translations.literal: " Senbian said: "The great army is only bound for Jing province; this city will naturally be no obstacle.
translations.idiomatic: " Senbian said: "The main army is bound for Jing province; this city will not stand in your way.

sentences.zh: 」騎去，頃之，執王珣等至城下，使說其弟琳。

translations.literal: " The horseman left; presently they brought Wang Xun and others under the wall and had them persuade his younger brother Lin.
translations.idiomatic: " The horseman left. Presently they brought Wang Xun and others to the wall to persuade his brother Lin.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「兄受命討賊，不能死難，曾不內慚，翻欲賜誘！

translations.literal: Lin said: "Elder brother, charged to punish the rebel, could not die in the crisis—he never blushed inwardly, yet now would offer me inducement!
translations.idiomatic: Lin said: "My brother was charged to punish the rebel, yet could not die in the crisis—he never blushed, and now would tempt me!

sentences.zh: 」取弓射之，珣慚而退。

translations.literal: " He took his bow and shot; Xun withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his bow and shot; Xun withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 景肉薄百道攻城，城中鼓噪，矢石雨下。

translations.literal: Jing pressed close on a hundred routes to assault the city; inside, drums and shouts rose, arrows and stones rained down.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pressed the walls on a hundred fronts; inside, drums roared and arrows and stones rained down.

sentences.zh: 景士卒死者甚眾，乃退。

translations.literal: Jing's soldiers died in great numbers; he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's men died in great numbers; he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 僧辯遣輕兵出戰，凡十餘返，皆捷。

translations.literal: Senbian sent light troops out to fight; in more than ten rounds all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian sent light troops out; in more than ten sallies he won every time.

sentences.zh: 景被甲在城下督戰，僧辯著綬、乘輿、奏鼓吹巡城，景望之，服其膽勇。

translations.literal: Jing wore armor below the wall directing battle; Senbian wore his sash, rode in a carriage, and had drums and pipes played as he circled the wall; Jing looked on and admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wore armor below the wall directing the fight; Senbian wore his sash, rode in a carriage, and had drums and pipes played as he circled the wall. Jing looked on and marveled at his nerve.

sentences.zh: 岳陽王察聞侯景克郢州，遣蔡大寶將兵一萬進據武寧，遣使至江陵，詐稱赴援。

translations.literal: Prince of Yueyang Cha, hearing Hou Jing had taken Ying province, sent Cai Dabao with ten thousand men to advance and seize Wuning, and sent an envoy to Jiangling falsely claiming he was coming to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cha of Yueyang, hearing Hou Jing had taken Ying province, sent Cai Dabao with ten thousand men to seize Wuning and sent an envoy to Jiangling falsely claiming he was coming to aid.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲答以侯景已破，令其退軍。

translations.literal: The assembly debated answering that Hou Jing was already broken and ordering him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated answering that Hou Jing was already broken and ordering him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹曰：「今語以退軍，是趣之令進也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi said: "If we now speak of withdrawal, we are urging him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong said: "If we tell him to withdraw now, we are urging him to advance.

sentences.zh: 」乃使謂大寶曰：「岳陽累啟連和，不相侵犯，卿那忽據武寧？

translations.literal: " He then had someone tell Dabao: "Yueyang has repeatedly declared alliance and mutual non-aggression—why do you suddenly hold Wuning?
translations.idiomatic: " He sent word to Dabao: "Yueyang has repeatedly pledged alliance and mutual non-aggression—why do you suddenly seize Wuning?

sentences.zh: 今當遣天門太守胡僧祐精甲二萬、鐵馬五千頓湕水，待時進軍。

translations.literal: We are now sending Tianmen Administrator Hu Sengyou with twenty thousand picked armor and five thousand iron horses to camp on the Jian, awaiting the hour to advance.
translations.idiomatic: We are sending Tianmen administrator Hu Sengyou with twenty thousand picked troops and five thousand iron horses to camp on the Jian, awaiting the hour to advance.

sentences.zh: 」察聞之，召其軍還。

translations.literal: " Cha heard this and recalled his army.
translations.idiomatic: " Cha heard this and recalled his army.

sentences.zh: 僧祐，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Sengyou was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏隴西襄公李虎卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wei Duke of Longxi Xiang, Li Hu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Li Hu, duke of Longxi Xiang in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 侯景晝夜攻巴陵，不克，軍中食盡，疾疫死傷太半。

translations.literal: Hou Jing attacked Baling day and night and could not take it; in the army food ran out, and pestilence killed and wounded more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing assaulted Baling day and night and could not take it. Food ran out in the camp, and pestilence killed or wounded more than half his men.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹遣晉州刺史蕭惠正將兵援巴陵，惠正辭不堪，舉胡僧祐自代。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Jinzhou Inspector Xiao Huizheng with troops to relieve Baling; Huizheng declined as unable and recommended Hu Sengyou in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent Jinzhou inspector Xiao Huizheng to relieve Baling. Huizheng declined and recommended Hu Sengyou instead.

sentences.zh: 僧祐時坐謀議忤旨繫獄，繹即出之，拜武猛將軍，令赴援，戒之曰：「賊若水戰，但以大艦臨之，必克。

translations.literal: Sengyou was then imprisoned for counsel that offended the ruler's intent; Yi at once released him, made him Fierce Martial General, and ordered him to the relief, admonishing him: "If the rebels fight on water, only press them with great ships and you will overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou was then in prison for counsel that had offended Yi. Yi released him at once, made him fierce martial general, and sent him to relieve Baling, warning him: "If the rebels fight on water, press them with great ships and you will break them.

sentences.zh: 若欲步戰，自可鼓棹直就巴丘，不須交鋒也。

translations.literal: If they wish land battle, you may simply beat the oars straight to Baqiu—no need to cross blades.
translations.idiomatic: If they want land battle, beat straight for Baqiu—no need to cross blades.

sentences.zh: 」僧祐至湘浦，景遣任約帥銳卒五千據白□脊以待之。

translations.literal: " Sengyou reached Xiangpu; Jing sent Ren Yue leading five thousand sharp troops to hold Bai□ Ridge and await him.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengyou reached Xiangpu. Jing sent Ren Yue with five thousand sharp troops to hold Bai□ Ridge and wait.

sentences.zh: 僧祐由它路西上，約謂其畏己，急追之，及於芊口，呼僧祐曰：「吳兒，何不早降！

translations.literal: Sengyou took another road west; Yue thought he feared him and pursued hotly; at Qian Mouth he called to Sengyou: "Wu boy, why not surrender early!
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou took another road west. Yue thought he feared him and pursued hard. At Qian Mouth he shouted: "Wu boy, why not surrender now!

sentences.zh: 走何所之！

translations.literal: Where are you running!
translations.idiomatic: Where do you think you are running!

sentences.zh: 」僧祐不應，潛引兵至赤沙亭；

translations.literal: " Sengyou did not answer, secretly led his troops to Chisha Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: " Sengyou did not answer and secretly led his troops to Chisha Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 會信州刺史陸法和至，與之合軍。

translations.literal: he met Xinzhou Inspector Lu Fahe arriving and joined armies with him.
translations.idiomatic: there he met Xinzhou inspector Lu Fahe and joined forces.

sentences.zh: 法和有異術，先隱於江陵百里洲，衣食居處，一如苦行沙門，或豫言吉凶，多中，人莫能測。

translations.literal: Fahe had strange arts; he had earlier hidden on Bailizhou at Jiangling; food, clothing, and dwelling were all like an ascetic monk's; sometimes he foretold fortune and disaster and mostly hit the mark—men could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe had strange arts. He had hidden on Bailizhou at Jiangling, living like an ascetic monk; he sometimes foretold fortune and disaster and mostly hit the mark—no one could fathom him.

sentences.zh: 侯景之圍台城也，或問之曰：「事將何如？

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the capital terrace city, someone asked him: "How will matters go?
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the terrace city, someone asked him: "How will this end?

sentences.zh: 」法和曰：「凡人取果，宜待熟時，不撩自落。

translations.literal: " Fahe said: "When ordinary men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; if you do not pluck it, it falls of itself.
translations.idiomatic: " Fahe said: "When men take fruit they should wait until it is ripe; leave it alone and it falls of itself.

sentences.zh: 」固問之，法和曰：「亦克亦不克。

translations.literal: " Pressed further, Fahe said: "He may overcome and he may not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: " Pressed further, Fahe said: "He may win and he may not win.

sentences.zh: 」及任約向江陵，法和自請擊之，繹許之。

translations.literal: " When Ren Yue marched on Jiangling, Fahe volunteered to strike him and Yi approved.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ren Yue marched on Jiangling, Fahe volunteered to strike him and Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，約至赤亭。

translations.literal: On renyin, Yue reached Chiting.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Yue reached Chiting.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲辰，僧祐、法和縱兵擊之，約兵大潰，殺溺死者甚眾，擒約送江陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Sengyou and Fahe loosed their troops and struck; Yue's army broke badly; killed and drowned were very many; they captured Yue and sent him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Sengyou and Fahe attacked. Yue's army collapsed; vast numbers were killed or drowned; they captured Yue and sent him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 景聞之，乙巳，焚營宵遁。

translations.literal: Jing heard this; on yisi he burned camp and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard this. On yisi he burned camp and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 以丁和為郢州刺史，留宋子仙等，眾號二萬，戍郢城；

translations.literal: He made Ding He Yingzhou Inspector, left Song Zixian and others, their host numbering twenty thousand, to garrison Ying city;
translations.idiomatic: He made Ding He Yingzhou inspector, left Song Zixian and others—twenty thousand in all—to garrison Ying city;

sentences.zh: 別將支化仁鎮魯山，范希榮行江州事，儀同三司任延和、晉州刺史夏侯威生守晉州。

translations.literal: detached general Zhi Huaren garrisoned Lushan, Fan Xirong acted for Jiang province, Masters of Protocol Ren Yanhe and Jinzhou Inspector Xiahou Weisheng held Jin province.
translations.idiomatic: detached general Zhi Huaren held Lushan, Fan Xirong acted for Jiang province, and masters of protocol Ren Yanhe and Jinzhou inspector Xiahou Weisheng held Jin province.

sentences.zh: 景與麾下兵數千，順流而下。

translations.literal: Jing with several thousand troops under his command went downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Jing went downstream with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丁和以大石磕殺鮑泉及虞預，沈於黃鶴磯。

translations.literal: Ding He killed Bao Quan and Yu Yu with a great stone pestle and sank them at Yellow Crane Rock.
translations.idiomatic: Ding He killed Bao Quan and Yu Yu with a stone pestle and sank them at Yellow Crane Rock.

sentences.zh: 任約至江陵，繹赦之。

translations.literal: Ren Yue reached Jiangling; Yi pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue reached Jiangling; Yi pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 徐文盛坐怨望，下獄死。

translations.literal: Xu Wensheng was charged with resentment and disaffection, imprisoned, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wensheng was charged with disaffection, imprisoned, and died.

sentences.zh: 巴州刺史余孝頃遣兄子僧重將兵救鄱陽，于慶退走。

translations.literal: Bazhou Inspector Yu Xiaoqing sent his elder brother's son Sengzhong with troops to rescue Poyang; Yu Qing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Bazhou inspector Yu Xiaoqing sent his nephew Sengzhong to relieve Poyang; Yu Qing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 繹以王僧辯為征東將軍、尚書令，胡僧祐等皆進位號，使引兵東下。

translations.literal: Yi made Wang Senbian Campaign-East General and Director of the Masters of Writing; Hu Sengyou and others all advanced in rank and title, and had them lead troops east.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made Wang Senbian campaign-east general and director of the masters of writing; Hu Sengyou and others were all promoted, and he had them lead troops east.

sentences.zh: 陸法和請還，既至，謂繹曰：「侯景自然平矣，蜀賊將至，請守險以待之。

translations.literal: Lu Fahe asked to return; once arrived, he told Yi: "Hou Jing will naturally be pacified; Shu rebels are about to come—please hold the passes and await them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fahe asked to return. Once back, he told Yi: "Hou Jing will fall of himself. Shu rebels are coming—hold the passes and wait.

sentences.zh: 」乃引兵屯峽口。

translations.literal: " He then led troops to camp at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then camped at the gorge mouth.

sentences.zh: 庚申，王僧辯至漢口，先攻魯山，擒支化仁送江陵。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wang Senbian reached Hankou, first attacked Lushan, captured Zhi Huaren, and sent him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Wang Senbian reached Hankou, stormed Lushan first, captured Zhi Huaren, and sent him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，攻郢州，克其羅城，斬首千級。

translations.literal: On xinyou, he attacked Ying province, took its outer wall, and beheaded a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, he attacked Ying province, took the outer wall, and took a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 宋子仙退據金城，僧辯四面起土山攻之。

translations.literal: Song Zixian withdrew to hold the Golden Wall; Senbian raised earthworks on four sides to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian withdrew to the Golden Wall; Senbian raised earthworks on every side.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史荀朗自巢湖出濡須邀景，破其後軍，景奔歸，船前後相失。

translations.literal: Yuzhou Inspector Xun Lang came from Chaohu through Ruxu to intercept Jing, broke his rear guard; Jing fled back, and ships before and behind lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou inspector Xun Lang came from Chaohu through Ruxu to intercept Jing and broke his rear. Jing fled back, and his fleet scattered.

sentences.zh: 太子船入樅陽浦，船中腹心皆勸太子因此入北，太子曰：「自國家喪敗，志不圖生，主上蒙塵，寧忍違離左右！

translations.literal: The crown prince's ship entered Zongyang inlet; trusted men in the ship all urged the prince to use this chance to go north; the prince said: "Since the state's ruin I have had no thought of living; the sovereign suffers dust—how could I bear to leave his side!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's ship entered Zongyang inlet. His trusted men all urged him to slip north. The prince said: "Since the state's ruin I have had no thought of living. The sovereign suffers exile—how could I leave his side!

sentences.zh: 吾今若去，乃是叛父，非避賊也。

translations.literal: If I go now, it is betraying my father, not avoiding the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: If I go now, I betray my father—I am not fleeing the rebel.

sentences.zh: 」因涕泗嗚咽，即命前進。

translations.literal: " He wept with running tears and at once ordered advance.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept aloud and ordered the ship forward.

sentences.zh: 甲子，宋子仙等困蹙，乞輸郢城，身還就景；

translations.literal: On jiazi, Song Zixian and the others were hard pressed and begged to surrender Ying city and return in person to Jing;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Song Zixian and the rest, hard pressed, offered to surrender Ying city and return to Jing in person;

sentences.zh: 王僧辯偽許之，命給船百艘以安其意。

translations.literal: Wang Senbian falsely agreed and ordered a hundred ships given to settle their minds.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Senbian feigned agreement and ordered a hundred ships provided to calm them.

sentences.zh: 子仙謂為信然，浮舟將發，僧辯命杜龕帥精勇千人攀堞而上，鼓噪奄進，水軍主宋遙帥樓船，暗江雲合。

translations.literal: Zixian thought it true, floated their boats to set out; Senbian ordered Du Kan leading a thousand sharp brave men to climb the parapet, drums and shouts bursting forward; naval commander Song Yao led tower ships, and on the dark river clouds of them closed in.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian believed him. As their boats were about to sail, Senbian ordered Du Kan with a thousand picked men up the wall in a sudden rush of drums and shouts; naval commander Song Yao closed on them with tower ships on the dark river.

sentences.zh: 子仙且戰且走，至白楊浦，大破之。

translations.literal: Zixian fought as he fled; at Baiyang Ford they were routed badly.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian fought as he fled. At Baiyang Ford Senbian broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 周鐵虎生擒子仙及丁和，送江陵，殺之。

translations.literal: Zhou Tiehu captured Zixian and Ding He alive and sent them to Jiangling, where they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tiehu took Zixian and Ding He alive and sent them to Jiangling, where they were executed.

sentences.zh: 庚午，齊主以司馬子如高祖之舊，復以為太尉。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Qi ruler, because Sima Ziru was an old companion of the High Ancestor, again made him Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Qi emperor, because Sima Ziru had been an old companion of the founding emperor, restored him as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 江安侯圓正為西陽太守，寬和好施，歸附者眾，有兵一萬。

translations.literal: Marquis of Jiang'an Yuanzheng was Xiyang Administrator, generous and mild and fond of giving; those who submitted were many; he had ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Yuanzheng of Jiang'an was Xiyang administrator—generous, mild, and open-handed. Many submitted to him; he had ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹欲圖之，署為平南將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi wished to scheme against him and appointed him Pacification-South General.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong meant to destroy him and appointed him pacification-south general.

sentences.zh: 及至，弗見，使南平王恪與之飲，醉，因囚之內省，分其部曲，使人告其罪。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Yi would not see him; he had Prince of Nanping Ke drink with him; when drunk, he imprisoned him in the inner bureau, divided his followers, and had someone announce his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Yi refused to see him. He had Prince Ke of Nanping drink with him; when Yuanzheng was drunk, Yi imprisoned him in the inner bureau, divided his followers, and published his crimes.

sentences.zh: 荊、益之釁自此起矣。

translations.literal: The feud between Jing and Yi began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The breach between Jing and Yi began here.

sentences.zh: 陳霸先引兵發南康，灨石舊有二十四灘，會水暴漲數丈，三百里間，巨石皆沒，霸先進頓西昌。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian led troops out from Nankang; Ganshi had twenty-four old rapids; it happened that the waters rose several zhang in a sudden flood; for three hundred li great stones were all submerged; Baxian advanced and halted at Xichang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian marched from Nankang. Ganshi had twenty-four old rapids; the river rose several zhang in a sudden flood and submerged the great stones for three hundred li. Baxian halted at Xichang.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒將伐柔然，突厥酋長土門邀擊，破之，盡降其眾五萬餘落。

translations.literal: Tiele were about to attack Rouran; Tujue chief Tumen intercepted and struck, broke them, and all their following of more than fifty thousand clans submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele were marching on Rouran when Tujue chief Tumen intercepted them, routed them, and took the submission of more than fifty thousand clans.

sentences.zh: 土門恃其強盛，求婚於柔然，柔然頭兵可汗大怒，使人詈辱之曰：「爾，我之鍛奴也，何敢發是言！

translations.literal: Tumen relied on his strength, sought marriage with Rouran; Rouran's Toubing Khan was greatly angered and sent a man to revile and insult him, saying: "You are my forge-slave—how dare you speak such words!
translations.idiomatic: Tumen, relying on his strength, sought marriage with Rouran. Rouran's Toubing Khan was furious and sent a man to revile him: "You are my forge-slave—how dare you speak such words!

sentences.zh: 」土門亦怒，殺其使者，遂與之絕，而求婚於魏；

translations.literal: " Tumen too was angry, killed his envoy, broke with them, and sought marriage with Wei;
translations.idiomatic: " Tumen too was angry, killed the envoy, broke with Rouran, and sought marriage with Wei;

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰以長樂公主妻之。

translations.literal: Wei Chancellor Tai gave him Princess Changle as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuwen Tai gave him Princess Changle as wife.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙亥，湘東王繹以長沙王韶監郢州事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yihai, Prince of Xiangdong Yi made Prince of Changsha Shao oversee Ying province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on yihai, Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made Prince Shao of Changsha oversee Ying province.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，侯景還至建康。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Hou Jing returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Hou Jing returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 于慶自鄱陽還豫章，侯瑱門拒之，慶走江州，據郭默城。

translations.literal: Yu Qing returned from Poyang to Yuzhang; Hou Zhen shut his gates against him; Qing fled to Jiang province and held Guo Mo's city.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing returned from Poyang to Yuzhang. Hou Zhen shut him out. Qing fled to Jiang province and held Guo Mo's city.

sentences.zh: 繹以瑱兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi made Zhen Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made Zhen Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 景悉殺瑱弟。

translations.literal: Jing killed all of Zhen's younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Jing killed all of Zhen's younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，王僧辯乘勝下湓城，陳霸先帥所部三萬人將會之，屯於巴丘。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Wang Senbian, riding victory, went downstream to Pencheng; Chen Baxian led his division of thirty thousand men intending to join him and encamped at Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Wang Senbian pressed his victory to Pencheng. Chen Baxian led thirty thousand men to join him and camped at Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 西軍乏食，霸先有糧五十萬石，分三十萬石以資之。

translations.literal: The western army lacked food; Baxian had five hundred thousand shi of grain and gave three hundred thousand shi to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The western army was starving. Baxian had five hundred thousand shi of grain and gave them three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅朔，王僧辯前軍襲于慶，慶棄郭默城走，范希榮亦棄尋陽城走。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day renyin of the month, Wang Senbian's vanguard raided Yu Qing; Qing abandoned Guo Mo's city and fled; Fan Xirong also abandoned Xunyang city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, the new moon, Wang Senbian's vanguard struck Yu Qing. Qing abandoned Guo Mo's city and fled; Fan Xirong abandoned Xunyang as well.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王僧振等起兵圍郡城，僧辯遣沙州刺史丁道貴助之，任延和等棄城走。

translations.literal: Prince of Jinxi Sengzhen and others raised troops and besieged the commandery city; Senbian sent Shazhou Inspector Ding Daogui to aid them; Ren Yanhe and the others abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sengzhen of Jinxi and others besieged the commandery city. Senbian sent Shazhou inspector Ding Daogui to help; Ren Yanhe and the rest abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹命僧辯且頓尋陽以待諸軍之集。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangdong Yi ordered Senbian to halt at Xunyang and await the gathering of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong ordered Senbian to halt at Xunyang until the armies gathered.

sentences.zh: 初，景既克建康，常言吳兒怯弱，易以掩取。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Jing had taken Jiankang, he often said the Wu men were timid and weak and easy to seize in a surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Jing took Jiankang, he often said the Wu men were timid and easy to overrun.

sentences.zh: 當須拓定中原，然後為帝。

translations.literal: He must first extend and settle the central plains, and only then become emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He must first win the central plains, and only then take the throne.

sentences.zh: 景尚帝女溧陽公主，嬖之，妨於政事。

translations.literal: Jing favored the emperor's daughter, Princess of Liyang, doted on her, and she hindered state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jing favored the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Liyang, doted on her, and she interfered in government.

sentences.zh: 王偉屢諫，景以告主，主有惡言。

translations.literal: Wang Wei remonstrated repeatedly; Jing told the princess; she had harsh words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei remonstrated again and again. Jing told the princess; she answered with harsh words.

sentences.zh: 偉恐為所讒，因說景除帝。

translations.literal: Wei feared being slandered by her and therefore urged Jing to remove the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei feared her slanders and urged Jing to remove the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及景自巴陵敗歸，猛將多死，自恐不能久存，欲早登大位。

translations.literal: When Jing returned defeated from Baling, many fierce generals were dead; he himself feared he could not long endure and wished to mount the throne early.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned defeated from Baling, many of his best generals were dead. He feared he could not last and wished to take the throne at once.

sentences.zh: 王偉曰：「自古移鼎，必須廢立，既示我威權，且絕彼民望。

translations.literal: Wang Wei said: "Since antiquity, shifting the cauldron has required deposition and installation—both to show our aweful authority and to cut off their people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei said: "Since antiquity, shifting the cauldron has required deposition and enthronement—both to show our power and to cut off the people's hope.

sentences.zh: 」景從之。

translations.literal: " Jing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing agreed.

sentences.zh: 使前壽光殿學士謝昊為詔書，以為「弟侄爭立，星辰失次，皆由朕非正緒，召亂致災，宜禪位於豫章王棟。

translations.literal: He had former Shouguang Hall academician Xie Hao draft an edict, stating that "younger brothers and nephews contended for the throne, the stars lost their order—all because I am not of the true line, summoning chaos and bringing disaster; the throne should be yielded to Prince of Yuzhang Dong.
translations.idiomatic: He had former Shouguang Hall academician Xie Hao draft an edict claiming that "nephews contended for the throne and the stars lost their order—all because I am not of the true line, summoning chaos and disaster. The throne should pass to Prince Dong of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 」使呂季略繼入，逼帝書之。

translations.literal: " He sent Lü Jilüe in next to force the emperor to write it.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Lü Jilüe in next to force the emperor to sign.

sentences.zh: 棟，歡之子也。

translations.literal: Dong was Huan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was the son of Huan.

sentences.zh: 戊午，景遣衛尉卿彭雋等帥兵入殿，廢帝為晉安王，幽於永福省，悉撤內外侍衛，使突騎左右守之，牆垣悉布枳棘。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Jing sent Commandant of the Guard Peng Juan and others leading troops into the hall, deposed the emperor as Prince of Jin'an, confined him in Yongfu Palace, removed all inner and outer guards, set nomad-cavalry guards to watch him, and planted thorn hedges on every wall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Jing sent commandant of the guard Peng Juan and others into the hall, deposed the emperor as Prince of Jin'an, and confined him in Yongfu Palace. He stripped all guards, set nomad-cavalry guards to watch him, and planted thorn hedges on every wall.

sentences.zh: 庚申，下詔迎豫章王棟。

translations.literal: On gengshen, an edict was issued welcoming Prince of Yuzhang Dong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, an edict welcomed Prince Dong of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 棟時幽拘，廩餼甚薄，仰蔬茹為食。

translations.literal: Dong was then under close confinement; his grain allowance was very thin; he lived on vegetables alone.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was then confined; his ration was meager; he lived on vegetables alone.

sentences.zh: 方與妃張氏鉏葵，法駕奄至，棟驚，不知所為，泣而升輦。

translations.literal: He was just hoeing melons with his consort Lady Zhang when the imperial equipage suddenly arrived; Dong was startled, knew not what to do, wept, and mounted the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was hoeing melons with his consort Lady Zhang when the imperial train suddenly arrived. Dong was startled, wept, and mounted the carriage.

sentences.zh: 景殺哀太子大器、尋陽王大心、西陽王大鈞、建平王大球、義安王大昕及王侯在建康者二十餘人。

translations.literal: Jing killed Lamented crown prince Daqi, Prince of Xunyang Daxin, Prince of Xiyang Dajun, Prince of Jianping Daqiu, Prince of Yi'an Daxin, and more than twenty princes and marquises in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing killed crown prince Daqi, Prince Daxin of Xunyang, Prince Dajun of Xiyang, Prince Daqiu of Jianping, Prince Daxin of Yi'an, and more than twenty princes and marquises in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 太子神明端嶷，於景黨未嘗屈意，所親竊問之，太子曰：「賊若於事義，未須見殺，吾雖陵慢呵叱，終不敢言。

translations.literal: The crown prince was bright in spirit and upright in bearing; toward Jing's faction he never bent his will; a close attendant secretly asked him; the prince said: "If the rebel still cares for righteousness, he need not kill me yet; though I insult and scold him, in the end he will not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was bright of spirit and upright in bearing; toward Jing's men he never bent. A close attendant asked him privately. The prince said: "If the rebel still cares for righteousness, he need not kill me yet. Though I insult and scold him, in the end he will not dare answer.

sentences.zh: 若見殺時至，雖一日百拜，亦無所益。

translations.literal: If the hour to kill me has come, though I bow a hundred times in a day, it will do no good.
translations.idiomatic: If the hour to kill me has come, a hundred bows in a day will do no good.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「殿下今居困□厄，而神貌怡然，不貶平日，何也？

translations.literal: " Another said: "Your Highness now dwells in dire □ distress, yet your spirit and face are at ease, not diminished from ordinary days—why?
translations.idiomatic: " Another asked: "Your Highness now dwells in dire □ distress, yet your spirit and face are at ease, undiminished from ordinary days—why?

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「吾自度死日必在賊前，若諸叔能滅賊，賊必先見殺，然後就死。

translations.literal: " The prince said: "I myself reckon my death-day must come before the rebel's; if my uncles can destroy the rebel, the rebel will be killed first, and only then will I go to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince said: "I reckon I must die before the rebel. If my uncles destroy him, he will be killed first, and only then will I die.

sentences.zh: 若其不然，賊亦殺我以取富貴，安能以必死之命為無益之愁乎！

translations.literal: If not, the rebel will also kill me to win wealth and honor—how could I take a life certain to die and spend it in useless grief!
translations.idiomatic: If not, the rebel will kill me anyway for wealth and rank—why spend a life already doomed on useless grief!

sentences.zh: 」及難，太子顏色不變，徐曰：「久知此事，嗟其晚耳！

translations.literal: " When disaster came, the prince's color did not change; he said calmly: "I have long known this—only regret it is late!
translations.idiomatic: " When the end came, the prince's color did not change. He said calmly: "I have long known this—only regret it came late!

sentences.zh: 」刑者將以衣帶絞之，太子曰：「此不能見殺。

translations.literal: " The executioners were about to strangle him with his sash; the prince said: "That cannot kill me.
translations.idiomatic: " The executioners were about to strangle him with his sash. The prince said: "That will not kill me.

sentences.zh: 」命取帳繩絞之而絕。

translations.literal: " He ordered them to take tent rope to strangle him until he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered tent rope—and died.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，棟即帝位。

translations.literal: On renxu, Dong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Dong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元天正。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed; the era name was changed to Tianzheng.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed; the era name was changed to Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 太尉郭元建聞之，自秦郡馳還，謂景曰：「主上先帝太子，既無愆失，何得廢之！

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Guo Yuanjian heard this, galloped back from Qin Commandery, and said to Jing: "The sovereign was the former emperor's crown prince and had no fault—how could you depose him!
translations.idiomatic: Grand commandant Guo Yuanjian heard this, galloped back from Qin commandery, and said to Jing: "The sovereign was the late emperor's crown prince and had no fault—how could you depose him!

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「王偉勸吾，云『早除民望』。

translations.literal: " Jing said: "Wang Wei urged me, saying 'Remove the people's hope early.'
translations.idiomatic: " Jing said: "Wang Wei urged me, saying 'Remove the people's hope early.'"

sentences.zh: 吾故從之以安天下。

translations.literal: I therefore followed this to settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I followed him to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 」元建曰：「吾挾天子令諸侯，猶懼不濟；

translations.literal: " Yuanjian said: "Holding the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords, I still fear failure;
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanjian said: "Holding the Son of Heaven to command the lords, I still fear failure;

sentences.zh: 無故廢之，乃所以自危，何安之有！

translations.literal: to depose him without cause is how one brings danger on oneself—what settlement is there!
translations.idiomatic: to depose him without cause is to court ruin—what settlement is there!

sentences.zh: 」景欲迎帝復位，以棟為太孫。

translations.literal: " Jing wished to welcome the emperor back and make Dong grand heir.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing wished to restore the emperor and make Dong grand heir.

sentences.zh: 王偉曰：「廢立大事，豈可數改邪！

translations.literal: Wang Wei said: "Deposition and installation are a great matter—how can they be changed again and again!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei said: "Deposition and enthronement are a great matter—how can they be changed again and again!

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He stopped.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，景又使使殺南海王大臨於吳郡，南郡王大連於姑孰，安陸王大春於會稽，高唐王大壯於京口。

translations.literal: On yichou, Jing again sent envoys to kill Prince of Nanhai Dalin at Wu Commandery, Prince of Nanjun Dalian at Gudu, Prince of Anlu Dachun at Kuaiji, and Prince of Gaotang Dazhuang at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Jing sent envoys to kill Prince Dalin of Nanhai at Wu commandery, Prince Dalian of Nanjun at Gudu, Prince Dachun of Anlu at Kuaiji, and Prince Dazhuang of Gaotang at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 以太子妃賜郭元建，元建曰：「豈有皇太子妃乃為人妾乎！

translations.literal: He gave the crown prince's consort to Guo Yuanjian; Yuanjian said: "How could a crown prince's consort become another man's concubine!
translations.idiomatic: He gave the crown prince's consort to Guo Yuanjian. Yuanjian said: "How could a crown prince's consort become another man's concubine!

sentences.zh: 」竟不與相見，聽使入道。

translations.literal: " In the end he would not meet her and allowed her to enter the Way.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he would not see her and allowed her to take vows.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，追尊昭明太子為昭明皇帝，豫章安王為安皇帝，金華敬妃為敬太皇太后，豫章太妃王氏為皇太后，妃張氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On bingyin, he posthumously honored the Luminous Heir as Emperor Zhaoming, the Peaceful Prince of Yuzhang as Emperor An, the Revered Consort of Jinhua as Grand Empress Dowager Jing, the Grand Consort of Yuzhang Lady Wang as Empress Dowager, and Consort Zhang as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, he posthumously honored the Luminous Heir as Emperor Zhaoming, the Peaceful Prince of Yuzhang as Emperor An, the Revered Consort of Jinhua as Grand Empress Dowager Jing, Lady Wang as empress dowager, and Lady Zhang as empress.

sentences.zh: 以劉神茂為司空。

translations.literal: He made Liu Shenmao Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He made Liu Shenmao minister of works.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，齊主如趙、定二州，遂如晉陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guisi, the Qi ruler went to Zhao and Ding provinces and then to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, the Qi emperor went to Zhao and Ding provinces and then to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 己亥，湘東王繹以尚書令王僧辯為江州刺史，江州刺史陳霸先為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On jihai, Prince of Xiangdong Yi made Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Senbian Jiangzhou Inspector and Jiangzhou Inspector Chen Baxian Eastern Yangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made director of the masters of writing Wang Senbian Jiangzhou inspector and Jiangzhou inspector Chen Baxian Eastern Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 王偉說侯景弒太宗以絕眾心，景從之。

translations.literal: Wang Wei urged Hou Jing to assassinate the Grand Ancestor to cut off the people's hearts; Jing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei urged Hou Jing to assassinate Emperor Jianwen to cut off the people's loyalty; Jing agreed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬寅夜，偉與左衛將軍彭雋、王修纂進酒於太宗曰：「丞相以陛下幽憂既久，使臣等來上壽。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the night of renyin, Wei with Left Guard General Peng Juan and Wang Xiuzuan brought wine to the Grand Ancestor, saying: "The chancellor, because Your Majesty has long been in hidden grief, sent us to offer longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the night of renyin, Wei with left guard general Peng Juan and Wang Xiuzuan brought wine to Emperor Jianwen, saying: "The chancellor, seeing Your Majesty long in grief, sent us to offer longevity.

sentences.zh: 」太宗笑曰：「已禪帝位，何得言陛下！

translations.literal: " The Grand Ancestor smiled and said: "The throne has already been yielded—how can you speak of 'Your Majesty'!
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Jianwen smiled and said: "The throne has already been yielded—how can you say 'Your Majesty'!

sentences.zh: 此壽酒，將不盡此乎！

translations.literal: This longevity wine—will it not be finished here!
translations.idiomatic: This longevity wine—you mean to finish me here!

sentences.zh: 」於是雋等繼曲項琵琶，與太宗極飲。

translations.literal: " Then Juan and the others in succession played the bent-neck pipa and drank to the utmost with the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: " Then Juan and the others played the bent-neck pipa in turn and drank with Emperor Jianwen to the end.

sentences.zh: 太宗知將見殺，因盡醉，曰：「不圖為樂之至於斯也！

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor knew he was about to be killed and therefore got fully drunk, saying: "I never imagined pleasure could reach this point!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen knew he was about to die and drank himself blind, saying: "I never imagined pleasure could reach this point!

sentences.zh: 」既醉而寢。

translations.literal: " When drunk he slept.
translations.idiomatic: " When he was drunk he slept.

sentences.zh: 偉乃出，雋進土囊，修纂坐其上而殂。

translations.literal: Wei then went out; Juan brought in an earth sack; Xiuzuan sat on it and the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei went out. Juan brought in an earth sack; Xiuzuan sat on it and the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 偉撤戶扉為棺，遷殯於城北酒庫中。

translations.literal: Wei took door panels for a coffin and moved the bier to the wine storehouse north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei used door panels for a coffin and moved the body to the wine storehouse north of the city.

sentences.zh: 太宗自幽縶之後，無復侍者及紙，乃書壁及板障，為詩及文數百篇，辭甚淒愴。

translations.literal: After the Grand Ancestor's close confinement he had no attendants or paper again; he wrote on walls and partition boards poems and prose of several hundred pieces, their words very mournful.
translations.idiomatic: After his confinement Emperor Jianwen had no attendants or paper; he wrote on walls and partition boards several hundred poems and essays, their words very mournful.

sentences.zh: 景謚曰明皇帝，廟號高宗。

translations.literal: Jing gave the posthumous title Emperor Ming and temple name High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing gave the posthumous title Emperor Ming and temple name High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 侯景之逼江陵也，湘東王繹求援於魏，命梁、秦二州刺史宜豐侯循以南鄭與魏，召循還江陵。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing pressed Jiangling, Prince of Xiangdong Yi sought aid from Wei, ordered Liang and Qin province inspectors Marquis of Yifeng Xun to give Nanzheng to Wei, and summoned Xun back to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing pressed Jiangling, Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sought aid from Wei, ordered Liang and Qin inspector Marquis Xun of Yifeng to yield Nanzheng to Wei, and summoned Xun back to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 循以無故輸城，非忠臣之節，報曰：「請待改命。

translations.literal: Xun, holding that to surrender a city without cause was not a loyal servant's conduct, replied: "Please await a revised order.
translations.idiomatic: Xun held that to surrender a city without cause was not a loyal man's conduct and replied: "Please await a revised order.

sentences.zh: 」魏太師泰遣大將軍達奚武將兵三萬取漢中，又遣大將軍王雄出子午谷，攻上津。

translations.literal: " Wei Grand Preceptor Tai sent Grand General Daxi Wu with thirty thousand men to take Hanzhong, and also sent Grand General Wang Xiong out through Ziwu Valley to attack Shangjin.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand preceptor Yuwen Tai sent grand general Daxi Wu with thirty thousand men to take Hanzhong and grand general Wang Xiong through Ziwu Valley against Shangjin.

sentences.zh: 循遣記室參軍沛人劉璠求援於武陵王紀，紀遣潼州刺史楊乾運救之。

translations.literal: Xun sent recorder Liu Fan of Pei to seek aid from Prince of Wuling Ji; Ji sent Tongzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent recorder Liu Fan of Pei to Prince Ji of Wuling for aid; Ji sent Tongzhou inspector Yang Qianyun to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 循，恢之子也。

translations.literal: Xun was Hui's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was Hui's son.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯等聞太宗殂，丙辰，啟湘東王繹，請上尊號；

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian and others, hearing that Emperor Taizong had died, on bingchen memorialized Prince Yi of Xiangdong and asked that he take the supreme title.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian and others, learning that Emperor Taizong was dead, on bingchen memorialized Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong and urged him to take the supreme title.

sentences.zh: 繹弗許。

translations.literal: Yi would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi would not consent.

sentences.zh: 司空、東道行台劉神茂聞侯景自巴丘敗還，陰謀叛景，吳中士大夫咸勸之；

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters Liu Shenma, hearing that Hou Jing had been defeated at Baling and was returning, secretly plotted to rebel against Jing; the gentry of Wu all urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and eastern-route mobile headquarters Liu Shenma, hearing that Hou Jing had been beaten at Baling and was retreating, secretly plotted rebellion; the gentry of Wu all urged him on.

sentences.zh: 乃與儀同三司尹思合、劉歸義、王曄、雲麾將軍元頵等據東陽以應江陵，遣頵及別將李佔下據建德江口。

translations.literal: He then joined with Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Yin Sihe, Liu Guiyi, Wang Ye, and Cloud-Banner General Yuan Yun and others to hold Dongyang in response to Jiangling, and sent Yun and detached commander Li Zhan downstream to seize the Jiande river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Yin Sihe, Liu Guiyi, Wang Ye, and Cloud-Banner General Yuan Yun and others in holding Dongyang to answer Jiangling, and sent Yun and detached commander Li Zhan downstream to seize the Jiande river mouth.

sentences.zh: 張彪攻永嘉，克之。

translations.literal: Zhang Biao attacked Yongjia and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao attacked Yongjia and took it.

sentences.zh: 新安民程靈洗起兵據郡以應神茂。

translations.literal: The people of Xin'an, Cheng Lingxi, raised troops and held the commandery in support of Shenma.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lingxi of Xin'an raised troops, held the commandery, and answered Shenma.

sentences.zh: 於是浙江以東皆附江陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon all east of the Zhe River submitted to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon everything east of the Zhe River submitted to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹以靈洗為譙州刺史，領新安太守。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Xiangdong made Lingxi Inspector of Qiao and concurrent Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong made Lingxi inspector of Qiao and concurrent administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙亥，王僧辯等復上表勸進，湘東王繹不許。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Wang Sengbian and others again submitted a memorial urging accession; Prince Yi of Xiangdong would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Wang Sengbian and others again urged accession; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong would not consent.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，繹以湘州刺史安南侯方矩為中衛將軍以自副。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Yi made Xiangzhou Inspector Marquis Fangju of Annan Central Guard General as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Yi made Xiangzhou inspector Marquis Fangju of Annan his Central Guard General and deputy.

sentences.zh: 方矩，方諸之弟也。

translations.literal: Fangju was Fangzhu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Fangju was Fangzhu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 以南平王恪為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Prince Ke of Nanping Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince Ke of Nanping inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景以趙伯超為東道行台，據錢塘；

translations.literal: Hou Jing made Zhao Bochao Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters and garrisoned Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing made Zhao Bochao eastern-route mobile headquarters and garrisoned Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 以田遷為軍司，據富春；

translations.literal: He made Tian Qian Army Secretary and garrisoned Fuchun.
translations.idiomatic: He made Tian Qian army secretary and garrisoned Fuchun.

sentences.zh: 以李慶緒為中軍都督，謝答仁為右廂都督，李遵為左廂都督，以討劉神茂。

translations.literal: He made Li Qingxu Commander of the Center Army, Xie Daren Commander of the Right Wing, and Li Zun Commander of the Left Wing, to campaign against Liu Shenma.
translations.idiomatic: He made Li Qingxu commander of the center army, Xie Daren commander of the right wing, and Li Zun commander of the left wing, to campaign against Liu Shenma.

sentences.zh: 己卯，加侯景九錫，漢國置丞相以下官。

translations.literal: On jimao, Hou Jing was granted the Nine Bestowals; the Han state established offices from Chancellor of State downward.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Hou Jing was granted the Nine Bestowals; the Han state established offices from chancellor of state downward.

sentences.zh: 己丑，豫章王棟禪位於景，景即皇帝位於南郊。

translations.literal: On jichou, Prince Dong of Yuzhang abdicated to Jing; Jing took the imperial throne at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Prince Dong of Yuzhang abdicated to Jing; Jing took the throne at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 還，登太極殿，其黨數萬，皆吹脣呼噪而上。

translations.literal: Returning, he ascended the Hall of Supreme Pole; his followers, tens of thousands, all pursed their lips and whooped as they went up.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he ascended the Hall of Supreme Pole; tens of thousands of his followers pursed their lips and whooped their way up the steps.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元太始。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was declared and the era name changed to Taishi.
translations.idiomatic: He declared a general amnesty and changed the era name to Taishi.

sentences.zh: 封棟為淮陰王，並其二弟橋、樛同鎖於密室。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Dong as Prince of Huaiyin and locked him together with his two younger brothers Qiao and Jiu in a secret chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Dong as Prince of Huaiyin and locked him in a secret chamber together with his younger brothers Qiao and Jiu.

sentences.zh: 王偉請立七廟，景曰：「何謂七廟？

translations.literal: Wang Wei asked to establish seven temples; Jing said, "What are seven temples?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei asked to establish seven ancestral temples; Jing said, "What are seven temples?

sentences.zh: 」偉曰：「天子祭七世祖考。

translations.literal: " Wei said, "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to seven generations of ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei said, "The Son of Heaven sacrifices to seven generations of ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」並請七世諱，景曰：「前世吾不復記，唯記我父名標；

translations.literal: " He also asked for the taboo names of seven generations; Jing said, "Earlier generations I no longer recall; I only remember my father's name Biao.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked for seven generations of taboo names; Jing said, "I no longer recall earlier generations; I only remember my father's name, Biao.

sentences.zh: 且彼在朔州，那得來啖此！

translations.literal: Besides, they are in Shuozhou—how could they come eat this!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, they are in Shuozhou—how could they come here to eat this!

sentences.zh: 」眾咸笑之。

translations.literal: " All laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " All laughed.

sentences.zh: 景黨有知景祖名乙羽周者；

translations.literal: Among Jing's followers was one who knew his grandfather's name was Yiyuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jing's followers was one who knew his grandfather's name was Yiyuzhou.

sentences.zh: 自外皆王偉制其名位，追尊父標為元皇帝。

translations.literal: Apart from that, Wang Wei devised all titles and ranks and posthumously honored his father Biao as Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Wang Wei devised every title and rank, and posthumously honored Jing's father Biao as Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 景之作相也，以西州為府，文武無尊卑皆引接，及居禁中，非故舊不得見，由是諸將多怨望。

translations.literal: When Jing was chancellor, he took Xizhou as his headquarters and received civil and military men without regard to rank; once he dwelt within the palace, none but old associates could see him, and many generals nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Jing had taken Xizhou for his headquarters and received civil and military men without regard to rank; once he lived within the palace, none but old associates could see him, and many generals nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 景好獨乘小馬，彈射飛鳥，王偉每禁止之，不許輕出。

translations.literal: Jing liked to ride a small horse alone and shoot at flying birds; Wang Wei constantly forbade him and would not allow him out lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Jing liked to ride out alone on a small horse and shoot at birds; Wang Wei constantly forbade it and would not let him go out lightly.

sentences.zh: 景鬱鬱不樂，更成失志，曰：「吾無事為帝，與受擯不殊。

translations.literal: Jing grew gloomy and joyless, further losing heart, and said, "I had no business becoming emperor—it differs little from being cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Jing grew gloomy and lost heart. "I had no business becoming emperor," he said. "It differs little from being cast aside.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，湘東王以長沙王韶為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Prince of Xiangdong made Prince Shao of Changsha Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the Prince of Xiangdong made Prince Shao of Changsha inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 益州長史劉孝勝等勸武陵王紀稱帝，紀雖未許，而大造乘輿車服。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosheng, Chief Administrator of Yizhou, and others urged Prince Ji of Wuling to declare himself emperor; though Ji did not yet consent, he greatly made imperial carriages and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Liu Xiaosheng of Yizhou and others urged Prince Ji of Wuling to declare himself emperor; though Ji had not yet consented, he was already building imperial carriages and regalia on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁未，謝答仁、李慶緒攻建德，擒元頵、李占送建康，景截其手足以徇，經日乃死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingwei, Xie Daren and Li Qingxu attacked Jiande, captured Yuan Yun and Li Zhan, and sent them to Jiankang; Jing cut off their hands and feet to display as warning, and after a full day they died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingwei, Xie Daren and Li Qingxu attacked Jiande, captured Yuan Yun and Li Zhan, and sent them to Jiankang; Jing cut off their hands and feet for public display, and after a full day they died.

sentences.zh: 齊主每出入，常以中山王自隨，王妃太原公主恆為之嘗飲食，護視之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Qi emperor went in or out, he always had the Prince of Zhongshan accompany him; the Princess of Taiyuan, his consort, constantly tasted his food and drink and watched over him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Qi emperor went in or out, the Prince of Zhongshan always accompanied him; the Princess of Taiyuan, his consort, constantly tasted his food and drink and watched over him.

sentences.zh: 是月，齊主飲公主酒，使人鴆中山王，殺之，並其三子，謚王曰魏孝靜皇帝，葬於鄴西漳北。

translations.literal: That month the Qi emperor made the princess drink wine, then had men poison the Prince of Zhongshan and killed him together with his three sons; he gave the prince the posthumous title Emperor Xiaojing of Wei and buried him north of the Zhang west of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Qi emperor made the princess drink, then had the Prince of Zhongshan poisoned and killed him together with his three sons; he gave the prince the posthumous title Emperor Xiaojing of Wei and buried him north of the Zhang west of Ye.

sentences.zh: 其後齊主忽掘其陵，投梓宮於漳水。

translations.literal: Later the Qi emperor suddenly opened his tomb and cast the outer coffin into the Zhang waters.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Qi emperor suddenly opened the tomb and threw the outer coffin into the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 齊主初受禪，魏神主悉寄於七帝寺，至是，亦取焚之。

translations.literal: When the Qi emperor first received the abdication, all Wei spirit tablets had been lodged at the Temple of Seven Emperors; now he took them out and burned them as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi emperor first received the abdication, all Wei spirit tablets had been lodged at the Temple of Seven Emperors; now he took them out and burned them too.

sentences.zh: 彭城公元韶以高氏婿，寵遇異於諸元。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao, Prince of Pengcheng, as a son-in-law of the Gao clan, received favor unlike other members of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao, Prince of Pengcheng, as a son-in-law of the Gao clan, received favor unlike the other Yuans.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司美陽公元暉業以位望隆重，又志氣不倫，尤為齊主所忌，從齊主在晉陽。

translations.literal: Palace Gate Commander of the First Rank Yuan Huiye of Meiyang, by rank and repute weighty and by temperament out of the common run, was especially feared by the Qi emperor and accompanied him at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gate Commander of the First Rank Yuan Huiye of Meiyang, weighty in rank and repute and odd in temperament, was especially feared by the Qi emperor and accompanied him at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 暉業於宮門外罵韶曰：「爾不及一老嫗，負璽與人。

translations.literal: At the palace gate Huiye cursed Shao, saying, "You are not the equal of an old woman, bearing the seal and giving it to another.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace gate Huiye cursed Shao: "You are not the equal of an old woman—bearing the imperial seal and handing it to another.

sentences.zh: 何不擊碎之！

translations.literal: Why not smash it to pieces!
translations.idiomatic: Why not smash it to pieces!

sentences.zh: 我出此言，知即死，爾亦詎得幾時！

translations.literal: I speak thus knowing I shall die at once—you too, how much longer have you?
translations.idiomatic: I speak thus knowing I die at once—you too, how much longer have you?

sentences.zh: 」齊主聞而殺之，及臨淮公元孝友，皆鑿汾水冰，沉其屍。

translations.literal: " The Qi emperor heard and killed him, and Yuan Xiaoyou of Linhuai as well; all were cut through the ice of the Fen River and their bodies sunk.
translations.idiomatic: " The Qi emperor heard and killed him, and Yuan Xiaoyou of Linhuai as well; all were cut through the ice of the Fen and their bodies sunk.

sentences.zh: 孝友，彧之弟也。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was Yu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou was Yu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 齊主嘗剃元韶鬢鬚，加之粉黛以自隨，曰：「吾以彭城為嬪御。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor once shaved Yuan Shao's temples and beard, applied powder and rouge, and kept him at his side, saying, "I take Pengcheng as my palace woman.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor once shaved Yuan Shao's temples and beard, applied powder and rouge, and kept him at his side, saying, "I take Pengcheng as my palace woman.

sentences.zh: 」言其懦弱如婦人也。

translations.literal: " He meant that Shao was timid as a woman.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant that Shao was timid as a woman.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝元皇帝上承聖元年（

translations.literal: Shizu, Emperor Xiaoyuan, first year of Chengsheng (
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, Emperor Xiaoyuan, first year of Chengsheng (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元五五二年）

translations.literal: renshen, AD 552)
translations.idiomatic: renshen, AD 552)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，湘東王以南平內史王褒為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Prince of Xiangdong made Wang Bao, Administrator of Nanping, Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Prince of Xiangdong made Wang Bao, administrator of Nanping, Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 褒，騫之孫也。

translations.literal: Bao was Qian's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was Qian's grandson.

sentences.zh: 齊人屢侵侯景邊地，甲戌，景遣郭元建帥步軍趣小峴，侯子鑒帥舟師向濡須，己卯，至合肥；

translations.literal: Qi men repeatedly raided Hou Jing's borderlands; on jiaxu, Jing sent Guo Yuanjian leading infantry toward Xiaoxian and Hou Zijian leading the fleet toward Ruxu; on jimao they reached Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Qi forces repeatedly raided Hou Jing's borders; on jiaxu, Jing sent Guo Yuanjian with infantry toward Xiaoxian and Hou Zijian with the fleet toward Ruxu; on jimao they reached Hefei.

sentences.zh: 齊人閉城不出，乃引還。

translations.literal: The Qi men shut the city and would not come out, so they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi shut the city and would not come out, so they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙申，齊主伐庫莫奚，大破之，俘獲四千人，雜畜十餘萬。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Qi emperor campaigned against the Kumo Xi and routed them, capturing four thousand men and more than a hundred thousand head of mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the Qi emperor campaigned against the Kumo Xi and routed them, capturing four thousand men and more than a hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 齊主連年出塞，給事中兼中書舍人唐邕練習軍書，自督將以降勞效本末及四方軍士強弱多少，番代往還，器械精粗，糧儲虛實，靡不諳悉。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor campaigned beyond the frontier year after year; Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and concurrent Palace Secretary Tang Yong mastered military documents; from commanders downward, the roots and branches of merit, the strength and numbers of troops in every quarter, rotations coming and going, the fineness of weapons, the fullness or emptiness of grain stores—none escaped his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor campaigned beyond the frontier year after year; Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and concurrent Palace Secretary Tang Yong mastered the military rolls—from commanders down, who had earned what, how strong every army in every quarter was, who rotated where, which weapons were fine or crude, which granaries full or empty; nothing escaped him.

sentences.zh: 或於帝前簡閱，雖數千人，不執文簿，唱其姓名，未嘗謬誤。

translations.literal: Sometimes before the emperor he would review troops; though they numbered thousands, without holding a register he would call out names and never err.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes before the emperor he reviewed troops; though they numbered thousands, without a register he called out names and never erred.

sentences.zh: 帝常曰：「唐邕強幹，一人當千。

translations.literal: The emperor often said, "Tang Yong is forceful and capable—one man equals a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, "Tang Yong is forceful and capable—one man equals a thousand.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「邕每有軍事，手作文書，口且處分，耳又聽受，實異人也！

translations.literal: " He also said, "Whenever there is military business, Yong writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ears at the same time—truly a strange man!
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Whenever there is military business, Yong writes with his hands, gives orders with his mouth, and listens with his ears at once—truly a strange man!

sentences.zh: 」寵待賞賜，群臣莫及。
